summary: Orbitcraft is an interactive strategy and simulation game that teaches players how to design, manage, and launch a complete space mission. Using NASA mission parameters and open datasets, Orbitcraft lets teams up to four members to collaborate in specialized roles (Science Lead, Systems Engineer, Flight Director, Comms Officer). Players select one or more mission objective, customize spacecraft components and scientific instruments, choose a launch vehicle and orbit, and try to balance strict limits on budget, mass, power, and data bandwidth connection. During live mission simulations, players respond to random spaceflight anomalies and receive scores during and after mission, and they will also receive overall mission engineering scorecard, explaining how every decision shaped their mission's scientific return and overall mission success.
details:
Orbitcraft is a browser-based strategy and simulation game where 1 to 4 players design, launch, and manage a space mission from concept to orbit. Players choose a mission objective (such as lunar ice mapping, solar storm monitoring, or exoplanet observation) and configure a spacecraft using real-world constraints. In multiplayer mode, teammates take on specialized engineering roles—Science Lead, Systems Engineer, Flight Director, and Comms Officer—while solo players manage all four subsystems. Every component choice dynamically affects mass, electrical power, budget, launch vehicle compatibility, and data downlink capacity. Once launched, players navigate a simulated mission timeline with random spaceflight anomalies and receive a detailed Post-Mission Scorecard explaining how their design choices impacted mission outcomes.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional aerospace education often isolates orbital mechanics from engineering trade-offs. Orbitcraft bridges this gap by showing students, educators, and space enthusiasts how real NASA mission teams balance competing requirements—such as sacrificing camera resolution to stay within launch mass limits. Our intended impact is to make systems engineering accessible, engaging, and intuitive for learners of all backgrounds while inspiring future STEM careers.

Tools, Languages & Software

• Frontend & Game Engine: React, TypeScript, HTML5 Canvas / Three.js for interactive 2D/3D spacecraft assembly and orbital visualization.

• Backend & Multiplayer: Node.js and WebSockets for real-time team collaboration.

• NASA Data & References: (as listed)

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Rather than a pure rocket-building sandbox, Orbitcraft focuses on collaborative systems engineering and real-time trade-off tension. Our team prioritized accessibility (zero-install browser gameplay), authentic physics-backed constraints scaled for fun 15-minute sessions, and clear visual feedback so players immediately understand why a mission succeeds or fails.
